title: Reinforcement Fine-Tuning for Reasoning towards Multi-Step Multi-Source Search in Large Language Models
abstract: This paper introduces R-Search, a novel single-LLM search framework that unifies multi-step planning, multi-source search execution, and answer synthesis within one coherent inference process. R-Search addresses the limitations of existing approaches by structuring its output into four explicitly defined components and employing a specialized Reinforcement Fine-Tuning (ReFT) method.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content:
Imagine you're trying to find information on a recent event. You would typically break down your search into smaller, manageable parts, and then use the results to answer your question. This is similar to how R-Search works. It uses a structured output format to guide the search process, ensuring that the model generates both accurate answers and reliable search plans.

This approach is made possible by a novel Reinforcement Fine-Tuning (ReFT) method, which optimizes the model's performance on multiple tasks simultaneously.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content:
R-Search uses a structured output format to generate reasoning traces, search plans, retrieved results, and final answers. The model is trained using a ReFT method that optimizes the expected reward over a dataset of query-answer pairs. The reward function evaluates the quality of the generated output based on three orthogonal dimensions: format compliance, DAG structural validity, and answer accuracy.

This approach enables the model to learn not only to generate correct final answers but also to produce well-structured, executable search plans that can be reliably parsed and executed by the environment.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content:
R-Search outperforms state-of-the-art methods on several benchmarks, including FinSearchBench-24 and SearchExpertBench-25. The model achieves a 70% reduction in context token usage and approximately 50% decrease in execution latency.

These results demonstrate the effectiveness of R-Search in enabling efficient and accurate search capabilities in large language models.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content:
R-Search has significant implications for real-world search applications, where users expect rapid and accurate responses. The model's ability to unify multi-step planning, multi-source search execution, and answer synthesis within one coherent inference process makes it an attractive solution for large language models.

Furthermore, R-Search's efficiency gains and reduced computational overhead make it a promising approach for time-sensitive applications.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content:
R-Search introduces several key innovations, including a novel ReFT method and a structured output format. The model's ability to generate well-structured, executable search plans and its efficiency gains make it a significant contribution to the field of large language models.

The use of a multi-component reward function and the integration of search planning with reasoning are also notable innovations.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content:
The code for R-Search is available at https://github.com/wentao0429/Reasoning-search. You can try out the model on your own benchmarks and explore its capabilities.

The model's efficiency gains and reduced computational overhead make it an attractive solution for large language models.
